title: Compliance: dos, don'ts and the final check
objectives: Apply the module's compliance rules to any rebalance.
Pass the trainer's final check: drift, methods, cheapest tools, target changes, behaviour and compliance.
body_md:
Do: agree the target mix and rebalancing rule in writing at the start. Explain that rebalancing controls risk and doesn't guarantee returns. Use new money first; check exit loads and possible tax; refer tax to a CA. Get the client's approval for each rebalance and record it. Keep rebalancing and target changes separate, each with its reason.

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Agree the target mix and rebalancing rule in writing at the start | Rebalance without a documented target |
| Explain that rebalancing controls risk and doesn't guarantee returns | Present rebalancing as a way to beat the market |
| Use new money first; check exit loads and possible tax; refer tax to a CA | Give tax advice or ignore costs |
| Get the client's approval for each rebalance and record it | Switch funds without consent, or to earn commission |
| Keep rebalancing and target changes separate, each with its reason | Change the target because of a market view or news |

> **Investor takeaway:** Standard disclaimer: mutual fund investments are subject to market risks; read all scheme-related documents carefully. Past performance does not guarantee future returns. Final check for trainers: a new joiner passes this module when they can explain why portfolios drift and what rebalancing does and doesn't achieve; measure drift against the client's target mix; choose calendar, band or a mix of both; rebalance in the cheapest way using new money first and checking exit loads and tax; tell rebalancing apart from changing the target mix; and handle reluctance to sell winners and buy losers, within compliance.
example: A trainee measures drift in points, picks calendar + band, uses new money first, checks loads and tax, and records approval — without promising returns.
say: Agree the target mix and rebalancing rule in writing at the start.
Get the client's approval for each rebalance and record it.
never: Switch funds without consent, or to earn commission.

o: “Rebalancing keeps your risk at the level you chose; it doesn't guarantee returns.”
check.why: “Rebalancing keeps your risk at the level you chose; it doesn't guarantee returns.” Explain the purpose honestly.

check.q: A trainee passes this module when they can:
o: Explain drift, measure it, choose a method, use the cheapest tools, separate target changes, and handle pushback within compliance
check.why: Final check: explain why portfolios drift and what rebalancing does and doesn't achieve; measure drift; choose a method; rebalance in the cheapest way; tell rebalancing apart from changing the target; handle reluctance, within compliance.

check.q: What must appear on all investor material for this module?
o: The fund's last month return only
